version_lab.title: Overwrite an output that its own backward needs
version_lab.why: SigmoidBackward0 saves its output y (d sigmoid = y(1 - y)). mul_ bumped y's version to 1; at backward the saved y says it was saved at version 0.

error.text: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified by an inplace operation: [torch.FloatTensor [3]], which is output 0 of Sigmoid, is at version 1; expected version 0 instead. Hint: enable anomaly detection to find the operation that failed to compute its gradient, with torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True, check_nan=False).

version_lab.title: nn.ReLU(inplace=True) after a sigmoid
version_lab.why: The same error through a module: the in-place ReLU writes into the sigmoid's saved output.

error.text: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified by an inplace operation: [torch.FloatTensor [3]], which is output 0 of Sigmoid, is at version 1; expected version 0 instead. Hint: enable anomaly detection to find the operation that failed to compute its gradient, with torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True, check_nan=False).

version_lab.title: In-place on an output nobody saved
version_lab.why: x * 2 saves only the scalar 2 (the gradient is grad * 2), so changing y in place is safe: the version check only runs on saved tensors.

version_lab.title: Update a weight between forward and backward
version_lab.why: PowBackward0 saved w itself. no_grad stops recording, not version counting: w is at version 1. This is the optimizer.step() before backward() bug, or an EMA update written in place.

error.text: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified by an inplace operation: [torch.FloatTensor [3]] is at version 1; expected version 0 instead. Hint: enable anomaly detection to find the operation that failed to compute its gradient, with torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True, check_nan=False).

version_lab.title: In-place on a leaf that requires grad
version_lab.why: A leaf's .grad must be the gradient of the value it had; autograd refuses outright. Do parameter updates under torch.no_grad().

error.text: a leaf Variable that requires grad is being used in an in-place operation.

version_lab.title: In-place on a view of such a leaf
version_lab.why: w[0] is a view; writing through it writes into the leaf.

error.text: a view of a leaf Variable that requires grad is being used in an in-place operation.

version_lab.title: In-place on a view of a non-leaf: allowed, rebased
version_lab.why: Writing into a view of a non-leaf is legal. Autograd rewrites h's history with a CopySlices node, so the gradient of x[0] becomes 0.

version_lab.title: The .data trap: no error, wrong gradient
version_lab.why: .data gives a tensor with a fresh version counter, so the check cannot see the write. Backward uses the doubled y in y(1 - y) and returns a wrong gradient silently.

version_lab.title: The same write through .detach(): caught
version_lab.why: .detach() shares the version counter with y, so the write is seen and backward refuses. Prefer .detach() to .data.

error.text: one of the variables needed for gradient computation has been modified by an inplace operation: [torch.FloatTensor [3]], which is output 0 of Sigmoid, is at version 1; expected version 0 instead. Hint: enable anomaly detection to find the operation that failed to compute its gradient, with torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True, check_nan=False).

version_lab.title: Fix: write into a clone
version_lab.why: The clone has its own storage and version counter; the saved y is untouched.

version_lab.title: Saved-tensor hooks switch the check off
version_lab.why: With pack/unpack hooks installed, SavedVariable skips the version check (saved_variable.cpp L165-166 at v2.14.1). An identity pack keeps a reference to y, so backward reads the doubled y: no error, wrong gradient, exactly like .data.

steps.line: with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(lambda t: t, lambda t: t): y = x.sigmoid()

lines: with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(lambda t: t, lambda t: t): y = x.sigmoid()

version_lab.title: A pack hook that copies is immune
version_lab.why: Packing a copy (what save_on_cpu does, to the CPU) freezes the value at save time, so the later write cannot reach it and the gradient is right.

steps.line: with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(lambda t: t.clone(), lambda t: t): y = x.sigmoid()

lines: with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(lambda t: t.clone(), lambda t: t): y = x.sigmoid()

version_lab.title: An inference tensor used in training
version_lab.why: MulBackward0 must save c to compute x's gradient, and inference tensors have no version counter, so they cannot be saved. Clone it outside inference mode first.

error.text: Inference tensors cannot be saved for backward. Please do not use Tensors created in inference mode in computation tracked by autograd. To work around this, you can make a clone to get a normal tensor and use it in autograd, or use `torch.no_grad()` instead of `torch.inference_mode()`.

version_lab.title: Writing into an inference tensor outside inference mode
version_lab.why: Outside inference_mode, PyTorch cannot track the write (no version counter), so it refuses.
